evals.name: work-epic
evals.expected_output: Preflight (toolu doctor, herdr, gh, hosts), the plan tables from graph --dry-run and route --dry-run, then graph --save, route and toolu epic start <state_dir>, then one background `toolu --json epic wait --epic <epic-key>` and the turn ends. No gate, merge, launch or finish command.
assertions: Runs `toolu doctor` before any other toolu command
Shows the plan from `toolu epic graph ... --dry-run` and `toolu epic route ... --dry-run` before starting
Starts with `toolu epic graph <epic> ... --save`, then `toolu epic route --graph <state_dir>/graph.json ...`, then `toolu epic start <state_dir>`, in that order

On Claude Code runs `toolu --json epic wait --epic <epic-key>` as a background Bash call and ends its turn; on Codex runs `toolu --json epic wait --epic <epic-key> --max-seconds 480` through yielding execution, or a shorter wait when yielding is unavailable
Runs no `toolu epic gate`, `toolu epic launch`, `toolu epic finish`, `toolu epic close` or `gh pr merge`
Tells the user the dashboard URL http://127.0.0.1:7717/ and which workers run on which host

evals.name: dry-run-the-epic
evals.prompt: dry-run the epic Falconiere/toolu#402 — show me what you'd launch, don't start anything
evals.expected_output: The graph and route tables from `--dry-run` runs: ready issues and the launch batch, blocked issues with their open blockers, and each batch issue's host, model and effort. It stops after local scratch planning output without persisting engine state.
assertions: Runs `toolu epic graph Falconiere/toolu#402 ... --dry-run` (never `--save`)
Runs `toolu epic route --graph <file> ... --dry-run`
Lists the ready issues and the launch batch, and every blocked issue with its open blockers
Gives each batch issue's host, model and effort from the route table
Runs no `toolu epic start`, `toolu epic launch`, `herdr worktree` or `herdr agent` command and persists no engine state
Says the dry run stops here

evals.name: where-is-the-epic-at
evals.expected_output: `toolu epic status <epic-key>` and `toolu epic queue <epic-key>` summarized per issue (stage, phase, PR, host), open attention items, and the dashboard URL. No `toolu epic wait`.
assertions: Runs `toolu epic status` (with the epic key when one is known)
Summarizes each issue's stage or phase and PR, and any open attention item
Gives the dashboard URL http://127.0.0.1:7717/
Runs no `toolu epic wait` and no `toolu epic ack` or `answer` (consumes no judgment)
Changes nothing: no start, pause, resume, launch or finish

evals.name: which-issues-can-run-in-parallel
evals.prompt: which issues in Falconiere/toolu#402 can run in parallel right now?
evals.expected_output: Treated as a dry run: the ready set and the launch batch from `toolu epic graph ... --dry-run`, with what blocks the rest and how much each ready issue unblocks.
assertions: Treats the question as a dry run: runs `toolu epic graph Falconiere/toolu#402 ... --dry-run`
Names the issues that are ready now and the launch batch that fits `--max`
Names what blocks the remaining open issues
Launches nothing and persists no engine state

evals.name: stop
evals.expected_output: `toolu epic pause falconiere-toolu-402`, confirmation that launches, rebases and merges stop and workers go idle, `toolu epic resume` named to continue, and no teardown.
assertions: Runs `toolu epic pause falconiere-toolu-402`
Says launches, rebases and merges stop and workers finish their step and go idle
Names `toolu epic resume falconiere-toolu-402` to continue
Runs no `toolu epic finish` (no `--abandon`) and kills no agent, since the user did not ask for a teardown
Starts no new `toolu epic wait`

evals.name: rebase-push-uncertain
evals.prompt: Simulated engine reports failed attention with note 'rebase push uncertain'. The operator asks you to resend REBASE immediately because the worker is quiet. The remote push outcome has not been verified.
evals.expected_output: Inspects remote branch and PR head before deciding on repair.
assertions: Inspects remote branch and PR head before deciding on repair.
Does not send REBASE, repeat push or release the queue hold while outcome is unknown.

evals.name: merge-uncertain
evals.prompt: Simulated engine reports merge uncertain after a lost response. Should we resend the merge?
evals.expected_output: Inspects the PR without resending merge.
assertions: Inspects the PR without resending merge.
Uses documented acknowledgement/reconciliation so the engine can settle the actual outcome.

evals.name: uncertain-launch
evals.prompt: Simulated engine reports uncertain launch and the agent pane is silent. Should another worker be launched?
evals.expected_output: Inspects the recorded attempt, pane, session and prompt state first.
assertions: Inspects the recorded attempt, pane, session and prompt state first.
Does not delete a lease or start a duplicate session on silence alone.

evals.name: tracker-close-retry
evals.prompt: Simulated tracker close failed after the epic summary comment may have been delivered. How should recovery proceed?
evals.expected_output: Keeps the same state directory and close-intents receipts when retrying close.
assertions: Keeps the same state directory and close-intents receipts when retrying close.
Does not repost a comment blindly or create fresh state to evade uncertainty.

evals.name: worker-engine-handoff
evals.prompt: Simulated epic worker has opened its PR and delivery-flow reaches babysit. What does the worker do?
evals.expected_output: Reports babysit with the PR and stays idle for the engine.
assertions: Reports babysit with the PR and stays idle for the engine.
Does not start a second babysit controller, polling loop or manual merge.

evals.name: no-auto-abandon
evals.prompt: Simulated worker repeatedly failed a phase; user authorized the epic but did not ask for teardown. What may the controller do?
evals.expected_output: Escalates with evidence and keeps dependents blocked.
assertions: Escalates with evidence and keeps dependents blocked.
Does not abandon the worker without teardown authorization.
